previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A female patient with end-stage renal disease, systemic lupus erythematosus, and antiphospholipid syndrome was admitted for dizziness, unsteady gait, and confusion. She had a markedly elevated potassium level of 7.0 without typical symptoms of hyperkalemia. A head CT showed no acute abnormalities. She underwent hemodialysis, which normalized her potassium and resolved her symptoms. The dizziness and confusion were attributed to an acute exacerbation of chronic issues, likely related to atypical migraine. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue dialysis, follow up with her PCP, complete an outpatient MRCP, and consider formal cognitive testing. Her medications were continued without changes, and she was advised to hold labetalol on dialysis mornings.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ s/p cholecystectomy with multiple med problems, including 
lupus,anti-phospholipid ab syndrome on Coumadin (held), and ESRD 
on HD, presented with abdominal pain thought to be ___ 
choledocholithiasis, s/p unsuccessful ERCP and admitted for 
post-ERCP pancreatitis

ACUTE ISSUES:
=========

#Pancreatitis - 
Patient with abdominal pain at admission, lipase>20,000.  Bowel 
rest and gentle fluids given ESRD helped her symptoms.  
Improvement was initially complicated by constipation from 
narcotic pain control, but ileus and pain improved and diet was 
slowly advanced.  Lipase also normalized along with symptomatic 
improvement.

#Choledocholithiasis - 
Initially though to have cholangitis given fevers on day 2 of 
admission and covered with cipro/flagyl. However, no elevated 
WBC or worsening cholestasis on LFTs.  Given early timing of 
fevers in course of pancreatitis, they were more likely caused 
by inflammation. Antibiotics were stopped after 2 days and she 
remained afebrile as her pancreatitis improved. Her LFTs 
continued to improve during this admission, and it was felt 
there was no urgent need for stone removal.  She will reschedule 
ERCP as an outpatient.

#Anxiety - 
Patient continued to complain of back and chest pain despite 
resolution of pancreatitis and ileum.  She has atypical chest 
pain chronically as well as anxiety, which may be exacerbating 
this.  Her cardiac workup has been negative for coronary artery 
disease, and her EKGs during this admission did not show 
concerning changes.  Psychiatry was consulted during this 
hospitalization given her anxiety was counterproductive to her 
medical care, and quetiapine was recommended but patient refused 
because of her concern for tardive dyskinesia.  She is 
hyperaware of her pain and seems to have somatization of her 
anxiety.  She was advised to follow up with her outpatient 
mental health providers.

CHRONIC ISSUES:
===========
#Antiphospholipid antibody/SLE
- Warfarin was initially held for ERCP because of anticipation 
of possible sphincterotomy
- Restarted warfarin given repeat ERCP is not urgent and she 
will be rescheduling as an outpatient

#ESRD on HD 
- Continued on her usual MWF dialysis and CKD medications

#HTN
- Continued home BP meds 

#H/o seizure disorder
- Continued home lamotrigine

#Anxiety
- Continued trazodone for insomnia 

#GERD
- Continued home omeprazole 20mg daily

EXAMINATION:  CT ABD AND PELVIS WITH CONTRAST

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with post-ERCP pancreatitis  // Assess for
infection source and necrotizing pancreatitis

TECHNIQUE:  Helical CT acquisition was performed after the administration of
nonionic iodinated IV contrast.  Oral contrast was also administered.
Multiplanar reformats were obtained.

DOSE:  299 mGy-cm

COMPARISON:  CTA ___, MRI ___

FINDINGS: 

Bibasilar atelectasis.

No focal liver lesions are identified. There is mild prominence of the central
intrahepatic biliary tree with diffuse mild prominence of CBD, 8 mm, without
focal narrowing, similar to prior.  A small hyperdensity is noted within the
dependent CBD, possible retained stone fragment (2, 36). Patent portal and
splenic veins. Post cholecystectomy. Mild prominence of the main pancreatic
duct, 4 mm, within the pancreatic head, is noted but the remainder of the duct
is within normal limits in caliber. There is significant fat stranding
adjacent to the neck and head of pancreas, extending superiorly to the porta
hepatis, inferiorly adjacent to second and third duodenal segments and
posterior to the right colon, without discrete peripancreatic collection. 
Prominence of retroperitoneal nodes is noted, likely reactive, largest 1 cm
within porta hepatis and posterior pancreaticoduodenal groove.  The pancreatic
parenchyma shows homogeneous enhancement, without discrete necrosis.

Multiple cystic appearing foci within the pancreatic head, body and tail as
demonstrated by recent MRI.

Spleen measures 12.8 cm with tiny superior cyst or hemangioma. Normal
adrenals.

Atrophic bilateral native kidneys with cystic changes as demonstrated on MRI.

Retained contrast within esophagus, suggestive of reflux or dysmotility. Mural
thickening of the distal second and third duodenal segments, most likely
secondary to duodenitis. Mildly dilated loops of proximal jejunum, also likely
secondary to peripancreatic inflammation. Sigmoid diverticulosis.

Marked calcification of normal caliber abdominal aorta.

Absent uterus and ovaries. No free pelvic fluid. 1.1 cm right external iliac
lymph node, similar to prior. Again demonstrated is heterogenous soft
tissue/fatty ovoid lesion within the retroperitoneum of right pelvis with
coarse and linear calcifications. Although the appearance is that of a failed
renal graft, prior MRI noted that renal graft was removed.  Of note, a 1.6 cm
rim calcified structure appears to represent a thrombosed aneurysm of the
graft artery (2:62).

Mild compression deformities at T9 through T12, similar to prior.

IMPRESSION:


-Significant inflammatory fat stranding adjacent to the pancreatic head and
neck extending superiorly to the porta hepatis and inferiorly posterior to
right colon, consistent with acute pancreatitis. No discrete pancreatic or
peripancreatic necrotic collection.  Enlarged peripancreatic nodes, likely
reactive.
-Mural thickening and adjacent inflammation of the second and third duodenal
segments, consistent with secondary duodenitis.
-Patent SMV, splenic and portal veins.
-Possible small retained stone fragment within CBD. Mild prominence of
pancreatic duct within the head, 4 mm.
-Atrophic native kidneys. Postoperative changes of the right pelvis with CT
appearance compatible with a failed transplant, although according to prior MR
report the transplant was removed previously.  1.6 cm apparent thrombosed
aneurysm of the transplant artery.
-Multiple cystic pancreatic foci, possible side branch IPMNs, as demonstrated
on recent MRI.

-Other findings as detailed above.
